Title: Spike: FDA recall system primer and data-limitations memo
Description: TIME BOX 2.5h - stop at the limit and log open questions. Research how FDA recalls work and what the enforcement-report data can and cannot represent. Primary sources only (fda.gov, ecfr.gov, openFDA docs). Do not rely on memory for regulatory citations; mark anything unconfirmed as UNVERIFIED.
Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Primer defines Class I / II / III recalls and voluntary vs FDA-requested/mandated recalls, each with a fda.gov or ecfr.gov URL
- [x] Primer summarizes 21 CFR Part 7 Subpart C (recall policy), drug cGMP (21 CFR 211) and food cGMP/preventive controls (21 CFR 117) at structure level, each with a CFR URL (Cornell LII mirror accepted; eCFR blocked automated access). Section-level citations re-verified in T6.2.1. [criterion amended 2026-11-16 with user approval]
- [x] Primer explains how a recall flows from firm initiation -> FDA classification -> enforcement report posting (mermaid diagram renders in a Markdown preview)
- [x] Section 'What this data cannot tell us' lists >= 6 limitations (e.g., no production-volume denominator, selection/classification bias, USDA-FSIS meat/poultry recalls not in openFDA, devices out of scope, report date != failure date, product-level vs event-level counting)
- [x] Every factual claim has a URL; `grep -c UNVERIFIED docs/domain/fda-recall-primer.md` is reported in the file footer
- [x] Time spent is logged at the bottom of the file and is <= 2.5h

Title: Define root-cause taxonomy v1 and QA glossary
Description: Draft 12-15 mutually exclusive root-cause categories for reason-for-recall text. Starting candidates (revise freely): microbial contamination; lack of sterility assurance; undeclared allergen; foreign material/particulate; potency/assay failure; dissolution/stability/OOS failure; chemical contamination/impurity (e.g., nitrosamines, mycotoxins); CGMP/process-control deviation; labeling error; packaging/container-closure defect; cross-contamination/mix-up; temperature/storage excursion or inadequate processing; unapproved/adulterated product (e.g., undeclared active ingredient); Other/Unclear. Map each to the FDA six-system drug inspection model (quality, facilities & equipment, materials, production, packaging & labeling, laboratory controls) or to a food hazard class (biological, chemical, physical, allergen). Flag mappings you are unsure about.
Acceptance criteria:
- [x] taxonomy.yaml loads with `python -c "import yaml;yaml.safe_load(open('data/reference/taxonomy.yaml'))"` and has 12-15 categories
- [x] Each category has: id, name, definition, >= 3 example phrases, inclusion rule, exclusion rule, applies_to (drug/food/both), system_or_hazard mapping
- [x] A single-label tie-break priority order is defined (e.g., allergen beats labeling) and documented with >= 5 worked conflict examples
- [x] An 'Other/Unclear' category exists with a rule limiting its use
- [x] glossary.md defines >= 25 terms incl. CAPA, OOS, cGMP, HACCP, HARPC/PCQI, FSMA, DMAIC, SPC, UCL/LCL, Pareto, Class I/II/III, NDC, FAERS
- [x] Unconfirmed mappings are marked UNVERIFIED

Description: Frame the project as a DMAIC cycle on the 'recall root-cause monitoring process' of a QA/regulatory function. Define every metric precisely before any code is written, including that 'recall rate' means recall EVENTS per month (no production denominator exists).

- [x] Table maps each project component to a DMAIC phase (Define=charter/CTQs; Measure=ingest+classifier+baseline; Analyze=Pareto/SPC/trend; Improve=QA action library; Control=control charts + watchlist)
- [x] CTQ tree lists >= 3 customer needs (e.g., timely detection, low false alarms, traceable evidence) with measurable specs
- [x] Metric dictionary defines >= 10 metrics each with formula, grain (event vs product), source field and caveat (incl. recall event, recall product, Class I share, severity-weighted count, risk score)
- [x] States explicitly which date field defines 'month' and why (default: report_date; sensitivity: recall_initiation_date)

Acceptance criteria:

Title: Build monthly category time series with defined date logic
Description: Complete month x category x product_type grid with zeros filled. Month = report_date (default). Exclude the current partial month. Build an alternate series on recall_initiation_date with the last N months truncated, N from the T2.1.3 lag P90, for sensitivity.

Title: Implement and validate control charts (c, p, Laney-adjusted) with run rules
Description: No production denominator exists, so use (a) c-chart on monthly event counts and (b) p-chart on category share of that month's events (handles overall volume swings), each with a Laney-style overdispersion adjustment when dispersion > 1. Phase I baseline window configurable (default 2015-01..2019-12): remove special-cause points iteratively, document each. Phase II monitors later months. Rules: point beyond 3 sigma; 8 consecutive points on one side of the centre line. LCL floored at 0.
Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Formulas verified against hand-calculated values on a toy dataset (tolerance 1e-9) in tests
- [x] Output has per category-month: cl, ucl, lcl, signal flag and rule id
- [x] Simulation: 1,000 stable Poisson series (n=60) give an empirical false-alarm rate for rule 1 and run rule, reported via record_metric
- [x] Charts for top 6 categories saved; signals marked and labeled with rule
- [x] Sensitivity: signal counts for 3 alternative baseline windows reported side by side
- [x] Docs state clearly that chart limits describe process stability of FDA-recorded recall activity, not firm quality

Title: Trend tests per category with multiple-comparison control
Description: Poisson GLM of monthly counts on time for trailing 60 months per category (switch to negative binomial if Pearson dispersion > 1.5). Report annual rate ratio with 95% CI and Benjamini-Hochberg q-values across categories.
Acceptance criteria:

- [x] Test: synthetic series with known 20%/yr growth recovers a CI that contains 1.20
- [x] BH correction applied (verified against statsmodels multipletests in test)

Title: Design and pre-register the risk score and flag rule
Description: Components (rank-percentile within product_type): momentum (trailing-12m vs prior-12m log rate ratio with 0.5 pseudo-count); severity (Class I share, trailing 24m); signal (count of SPC rule violations in trailing 6m); breadth (1 - share of the largest single firm; penalizes single-firm artifacts); volume (log trailing-12m events). Default weights 0.35/0.25/0.20/0.10/0.10 chosen a priori and justified in the doc. Flag = top-quartile score AND momentum > 0 AND trailing-12m events >= 10. Write the evaluation plan and success criteria in the doc and commit it BEFORE running T5.1.2 (pre-registration).
Acceptance criteria:
- [x] risk-score.md contains formulas, weights, justification, flag rule, and a dated 'pre-registration' section committed before T5.1.2 starts
- [x] Weights sum to 1.0 (test)
- [x] Toy-data score matches a hand-computed value (test)
- [x] Score table by category x month x product_type is produced; each row names its top contributing component
- [x] Minimum-volume guard demonstrably suppresses a flag in a small-count test case

Title: Rolling-origin backtest versus naive baselines
Description: Origins every 6 months from 2016-06 to latest minus 12 months. At each origin compute scores using ONLY data up to the origin; outcome = next-12-month log change in event count and Class I share, per category x product_type. Baselines: B1 rank by trailing-12m volume; B2 momentum only; B3 random (permutation). Use non-overlapping 12-month-spaced origins for inference and block bootstrap by year; 6-monthly origins are descriptive only. Be explicit about regression to the mean.
Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Leakage test: score at an origin is identical when all rows after the origin are deleted
- [x] Reported: Spearman rho (score vs outcome) with block-bootstrap 95% CI; precision@3 vs B1/B2/B3 with permutation p-values
- [x] TARGET (not an achieved result): precision@3 exceeds best baseline by >= 0.15 and rho CI excludes 0. If missed, reports/backtest.md says so plainly and the README framing changes accordingly
- [x] Number of origins and units is stated next to every statistic
- [x] All numbers recorded through record_metric with label 'achieved'

Title: Sensitivity analysis: weights, windows, label noise
Description: (a) 1,000 Dirichlet(1,...,1) weight draws -> distribution of each category's rank; (b) trailing-window length 6/12/24 months; (c) inject random label noise at the classifier's measured error rate and re-rank. Output a per-category 'flag stability' (% of runs in which it stays flagged).
Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Median Kendall tau vs default ranking reported (TARGET >= 0.70)
- [x] Per-category flag-stability table written to reports/tables/flag_stability.csv
- [x] Rank-stability chart saved
- [x] Fragile flags (<60% stability) are named in the report
